author: @simplifyinai
summary: dots.ocr is a single vision-language model that does document layout detection and content recognition in one pass: it returns each block's bounding box and category with its text, tables as HTML, formulas as LaTeX, and prose as Markdown, in reading order, across 100+ languages. The 1.7B is the language-model foundation; the full model is about 3.0B parameters including the vision encoder, weights about 6 GB in BF16. Released 2025-07-30. A successor line, dots.mocr (rebranded from dots.ocr-1.5 on 2026-03-19), extends the same base to structured-graphics-to-SVG parsing. License MIT, free for commercial use. Use: clone the repo, Python 3.12 / torch 2.7.0 / CUDA 12.8, pip install -e ., download weights via the repo script, or pull the official Docker image built on vLLM; integrated into vLLM since v0.11.0; task switching is by prompt. Plugs into three live lanes: the book-scanning queue (local, free, single-model page parser), the MarkItDown document-conversion lane (candidate front end where the PDF path is weak on layout, tables, and formulas), and the Firecrawl v2 migration test (native LaTeX output makes it the offline control for the LaTeX-preservation check). Risks: the repo warns of endless repetition on runs of ellipses/underscores, pictures are not parsed, and it is not yet optimised for high-volume PDF work; weights have not updated since 2025-10-31 per secondary coverage; benchmark leadership claims are the authors' and launch coverage's numbers, verified as published, not independently reproduced.
metrics_or_datasets: OmniDocBench SOTA at its size (authors' claim)
88.6 table TEDS vs 85.8 for Gemini 2.5 Pro (launch coverage)
engine_training_value: Direct and concrete. Parsed pages are labelled training material: block category plus bounding box plus text plus table structure plus formula LaTeX, produced locally from Garrett's own corpus (papers, books, stat PDFs). The model's own dots.ocr-bench (1,493 pages, 100 languages) is a labelled evaluation set for the parsing lane. For the prediction engine itself the value is indirect but real: every PDF in the corpus becomes machine-readable features instead of prose.
provenance: Poster @simplifyinai is the summarizer/recreator; origin is the RedNote (Xiaohongshu) HI Lab model itself. Primary sources verified this run: repo README read via raw source, Hugging Face weights page.

author: @gittrend.io
title_or_hook: Chronicles of the Realm (jiangshan-map), interactive historical atlas of China
summary: An interactive historical atlas of China spanning 403 BCE to the present: 2,400+ years, 18 historical periods, 198 territory snapshots, rendered as one parchment-style map with a draggable timeline. Beyond territory it carries ancient-city and strategic-pass genealogy cards (Trace Place), person chronicles that follow historical figures across time and space, poetic/battlefield landmarks, and reigning-monarch/era layers. The README also claims out-of-the-box use as a visualisation engine for LLMs, MCP clients, and AI agents (README-level only this run; the repo tree and MCP surface were not deep-read). License GPL-3.0: study and learn freely, but code reuse into a proprietary surface carries GPL obligations; one data layer (prefecture boundaries via CHGIS) is explicitly not under GPL and is non-commercial/educational only. Boundaries are schematic approximations checked against scholarly texts; the repo itself says do not cite them as precise. Plugs into the GSE customer-facing front end as a pattern, not a product: timeline-scrub plus place-genealogy plus person-trajectory in one canvas, with the URL mirroring the view. Self-hosting is from source (JavaScript project); the hosted demo needs no account.
metrics_or_datasets: star counts disagree across trackers, about 7.7K-8.4K in the last day (secondary-source noise)
verdict: LEARN-ONLY (pattern), WATCH on the MCP claim
engine_training_value: none for the prediction engine - context only. Its bundled data (198 labelled territory snapshots, place genealogies) is a clean example of time-indexed state data design, useful as a schema reference for season-state storage, not as training data.
provenance: Poster @gittrend.io is the summarizer/recreator; origin is the repo itself. Primary source located this run: repo and live demo; GPL-3.0 licence verified.

author: @alexandr
title_or_hook: Muse Try On launches inside Muse shopping
summary: Muse, the Meta personal-agent product Garrett is using to run this sweep, now offers Try On while shopping: when a user is shopping for clothing, Muse proactively offers to show how the item would look on them before they buy. Announced Nov 18, 2026, the day before this run, by Alexandr Wang (Meta Chief AI Officer) and the Muse account. Corroborated this run by multiple same-day reports (All Things Muse, RuntimeWire, WittyWires, ChasingNext), all tracing to Wang's X post and the Muse account's own post. One report adds that Meta says Muse's shopping agent passed 10 million users in the US and Canada by late October; that figure is Meta's claim as reported, UNVERIFIED independently. No install or repo: it is a feature inside Muse's shopping flow; availability/rollout detail was not specified in Wang's post. This workspace already carries a style_tryon skill (show the user wearing items from shopping results, rendered from their own photo, then help them buy the pick); this announcement is that same capability arriving as a native, proactive Muse feature. A visual preview is not a fit measurement. No agent action taken; nothing was shopped or bought in this run.
metrics_or_datasets: Muse shopping agent passed 10 million users in US and Canada by late October (Meta claim via one report, UNVERIFIED)
engine_training_value: none - context only for the prediction engine. For the shopping lane, try-on accept/decline and purchase-after-preview outcomes would be labelled preference data, but no such data was collected here.
provenance: Poster @alexandr is Alexandr Wang, Meta Chief AI Officer; this is a launch announcement, not a recreator summary; origin is Meta's Muse itself. Corroborated this run by four same-day reports tracing to the two origin posts.
